mechanism_claim: False-negative non-picks that become large winners exhibit compressed near-buy-point geometry: low px_vs_ma50 (<6%), modest mom_20 (<8%), and shallow pullback depth (<=-7.3%), producing a tight consolidation state that B0's selection criteria reject but which subsequently resolves into large winners.

falsifiable_predictions: In a validation sample, among non-B0-pick entities where px_vs_ma50 < 0.06 AND mom_20 < 0.08 AND vol_ratio_5_20 < 1.2, the large_win rate will be >= 35%, significantly exceeding the base rate for all non-picks

If a false-negative entity has compressed px_vs_ma50 < 0.05 but subsequently drops below its 50-day MA (px_vs_ma50 < 0) within 4 weeks of snapshot, the w4_return_bucket will NOT be large_win with >80% confidence

The vol_ratio_5_20 threshold of 1.2 distinguishes false-negative big winners from false-negative relative winners: FN large_win entities will have median vol_ratio < 1.2, while FN small_win entities will have median vol_ratio > 1.3
Entities with pullback_pct < -15 (deeper than FN median) but still non-picked will have lower large_win rates than entities with pullback_pct between -5 and -10, controlling for mom_20 and px_vs_ma50
policy_implications: B0 selection criteria may systematically reject valid setups by penalizing compressed near-buy-point geometry; relaxing px_vs_ma50 thresholds from current values to <0.10 could recover some false negatives
Adding a secondary filter for compressed-geometry non-picks could create a supplemental watchlist tier with independent signal generation, reducing correlation with primary B0 selections

Volume confirmation becomes critical for compressed-geometry picks: low vol_ratio_5_20 (<1.2) appears to identify stealth accumulation, while elevated vol_ratio may indicate distribution rather than base-building

The shallow-pullback false negatives (entity_de1c657364, entity_05b4c6b1f7) suggest tighter stop-loss placement is viable for this pattern since the compression itself signals limited downside from entry point
